verdict.rationale: Bun documents a relocatable global install cache via `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR`, a mode that never touches the network and errors if a dependency is not cached, `--frozen-lockfile` for reproducible installs, and large install-speed claims. Together these give the building blocks for fast, offline-capable CI installs. However, no CI-specific cache-restore setup (e.g., a documented save/restore cache step or recipe) appears in the evidence. missing for 10: a documented CI cache-restore recipe/workflow, independent hands-on corroboration of CI speed and offline install behavior.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can make CI installs fast with a documented cache-restore setup and offline-capable installs

citations.quote: Bun stores every package downloaded from the registry in a global cache at `~/.bun/install/cache`, or the path set by the `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` environment variable.
Never touch the network (registry, tarball URLs, git); a required dependency that is not cached is an error
For reproducible installs, use `--frozen-lockfile`. Bun installs the exact versions specified in the lockfile and does not update it.
Switch from `npm install` to `bun install` in any Node.js project to make your installations up to 25x faster.
